pr.title: FEATURE: Can edit category/host relationships for embedding

raw_findings.body: `execute(...)[0]` raises (IndexError/NoMethodError on nil) before the embeddable_hosts branch is even reached, aborting the migration and blocking deploys for the common case of sites that never set embed_category.
raw_findings.evidence:
category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c
                        INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name
                        WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i
raw_findings.failure_mode: Migration raises and fails on sites without an embed_category setting row.
raw_findings.impact: `execute(...)[0]` raises (IndexError/NoMethodError on nil) before the embeddable_hosts branch is even reached, aborting the migration and blocking deploys for the common case of sites that never set embed_category.
raw_findings.root_cause: Unconditional indexing of a query result that can legitimately be empty.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Guard the result set: fetch the rows, and only call `['id'].to_i` when `cmd_tuples > 0` (mirroring the guard used for `embeddable_hosts` below), falling back to the uncategorized category id otherwise.
raw_findings.title: Migration crashes when 'embed_category' site setting row does not exist
raw_findings.trigger: Running `rake db:migrate` on any site that never customized the `embed_category` site setting (settings are only persisted when changed from default), so the SELECT returns zero rows.

raw_findings.body: Rows are inserted verbatim (raw SQL skips the model's before_validation that strips `https?://` and paths), so `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` comparing `lower(host) = <uri.host>` never matches; embedding silently stops working for those hosts after the migration.
raw_findings.evidence: execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
raw_findings.failure_mode: Previously-working embed hosts are rejected as invalid referers after upgrading.
raw_findings.impact: Rows are inserted verbatim (raw SQL skips the model's before_validation that strips `https?://` and paths), so `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` comparing `lower(host) = <uri.host>` never matches; embedding silently stops working for those hosts after the migration.
raw_findings.root_cause: Data migration inserts via raw SQL without replicating the normalization the new model relies on for lookups.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize each value in the migration before inserting (strip `^https?://` and any trailing path), matching the model's before_validation behavior.
raw_findings.title: Migration copies raw host strings (with scheme/path) that bypass model normalization, breaking host matching
raw_findings.trigger: A site whose old `embeddable_hosts` setting contains entries with a scheme or path (e.g. 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234'), which the old `allows_embeddable_host?` explicitly supported by stripping the scheme before comparing.

raw_findings.body: The interpolated INSERT statement becomes malformed (or executes unintended SQL), aborting the migration mid-run.
raw_findings.evidence: execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
raw_findings.failure_mode: Migration fails or executes corrupted SQL for hosts containing quote characters.
raw_findings.impact: The interpolated INSERT statement becomes malformed (or executes unintended SQL), aborting the migration mid-run.
raw_findings.root_cause: Unescaped string interpolation of stored data into an executed SQL statement.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Quote the value with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` (or use exec_params/sanitized insert) instead of string interpolation.
raw_findings.title: Migration interpolates setting-derived host string directly into SQL
raw_findings.trigger: The old `embeddable_hosts` site-setting value contains a single quote or other SQL metacharacter in one of its newline-separated entries.

raw_findings.body: `lower(host)` on the column is compared to the case-preserved parameter, so a legitimately allowed host with uppercase letters in the referer is rejected and embedding fails with 'invalid referer host'.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Valid embed requests are denied depending on referer host casing.
raw_findings.impact: `lower(host)` on the column is compared to the case-preserved parameter, so a legitimately allowed host with uppercase letters in the referer is rejected and embedding fails with 'invalid referer host'.
raw_findings.root_cause: Only one side of the case-insensitive comparison is normalized.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Downcase the parameter as well: `where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase)`.
raw_findings.title: record_for_host compares lowercased column against non-downcased referer host
raw_findings.trigger: A referer or embed URL with mixed-case host, e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com/post`; Ruby's URI#host preserves the original casing.

raw_findings.body: `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError before validations run, producing a 500 error instead of the expected validation failure from `validates_format_of`.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Server error instead of a graceful validation error for blank hosts.
raw_findings.impact: `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError before validations run, producing a 500 error instead of the expected validation failure from `validates_format_of`.
raw_findings.root_cause: Normalization callback assumes the attribute is always a non-nil string.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Guard the normalization, e.g. `if self.host.present?` around the `sub!` calls so validation can report the missing host normally.
raw_findings.title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
raw_findings.trigger: Validating or saving an EmbeddableHost whose `host` attribute is nil (e.g. an API/admin request omitting the host param, or calling `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?`).

raw_findings.body: The record fails validation and the admin cannot whitelist a perfectly valid embedding host, even though the old free-text setting accepted it.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Legitimate hosts are rejected during create/update.
raw_findings.impact: The record fails validation and the admin cannot whitelist a perfectly valid embedding host, even though the old free-text setting accepted it.
raw_findings.root_cause: Hard-coded `{2,5}` TLD length in the new format validation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Relax the TLD length bound (e.g. `[a-z]{2,}`) or use a proper hostname validation instead of a fixed-length TLD class.
raw_findings.title: Host validation regex rejects valid TLDs longer than 5 characters
raw_findings.trigger: An admin adds a host with a TLD longer than 5 characters, e.g. `example.museum` or any new gTLD like `site.photography`.

raw_findings.body: `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for the missing id, so the resulting plural array contains `undefined` holes while `delete obj[k]` discards the original ids — data is silently lost, unlike the singular branch which preserves `obj[k]` when hydration fails. Also `hydrated || []` is dead code since `map` never returns a falsy value.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Models expose arrays with undefined members and lose the raw id list when side-loaded data is incomplete.
raw_findings.impact: `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for the missing id, so the resulting plural array contains `undefined` holes while `delete obj[k]` discards the original ids — data is silently lost, unlike the singular branch which preserves `obj[k]` when hydration fails. Also `hydrated || []` is dead code since `map` never returns a falsy value.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new array branch omits the existence check the singular branch performs before replacing the key.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Filter out failed lookups (e.g. `.filter(h => h)`) or only assign/delete when all ids hydrated, mirroring the singular `if (hydrated)` guard; drop the meaningless `|| []`.
raw_findings.title: Plural _ids hydration inserts undefined entries and unconditionally deletes the ids key on lookup failure
raw_findings.trigger: A `__rest_serializer: "1"` response contains a `*_ids` array referencing an id that is missing from the side-loaded collection in the payload root.

raw_findings.body: `host` is nil, so `save_host` calls `host.host =` on nil and raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 instead of a 404/JSON error.
raw_findings.impact: `host` is nil, so `save_host` calls `host.host =` on nil and raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 instead of a 404/JSON error.
raw_findings.root_cause: Missing nil handling after a `.where(...).first` lookup.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` (404 via RecordNotFound) or return `render_json_error` / raise Discourse::NotFound when the record is missing.
raw_findings.title: EmbeddableHostsController#update raises NoMethodError for unknown id
raw_findings.trigger: PUT /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with an id that no longer exists (e.g. deleted in another tab).

raw_findings.body: `host` is nil and `host.destroy` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a clean 404 response.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled 500 error on double-delete or stale ids.
raw_findings.impact: `host` is nil and `host.destroy` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a clean 404 response.
raw_findings.root_cause: Missing nil handling after a `.where(...).first` lookup.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use `find` or guard the nil case before calling `destroy`, returning Discourse::NotFound when missing.
raw_findings.title: EmbeddableHostsController#destroy raises NoMethodError for unknown id
raw_findings.trigger: DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id for an id that does not exist (e.g. already deleted).

raw_findings.body: The two fabricator files' names contradict their contents — category_fabricator.rb defines :embeddable_host while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines :category and friends — violating the one-fabricator-per-named-file convention and misleading future maintenance.
raw_findings.failure_mode: File names no longer indicate their contents, confusing spec maintenance.
raw_findings.impact: The two fabricator files' names contradict their contents — category_fabricator.rb defines :embeddable_host while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines :category and friends — violating the one-fabricator-per-named-file convention and misleading future maintenance.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new fabricator was accidentally written into the existing category fabricator file and the category fabricators moved into the new file.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Swap the contents back: keep the category fabricators in category_fabricator.rb and put only the :embeddable_host fabricator in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.
raw_findings.title: Fabricator contents swapped: category_fabricator.rb now defines the embeddable_host fabricator
raw_findings.trigger: Any developer looking for the category fabricators (now living in the new spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb) or the embeddable_host fabricator (now in category_fabricator.rb).

raw_findings.body: Duplicated filters run twice (or at minimum add dead declarations), diverging from every other Admin::AdminController subclass in the codebase and inviting confusion about where auth is enforced. The same duplication exists in Admin::EmbeddingController.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent, redundant authorization declarations across admin controllers.
raw_findings.impact: Duplicated filters run twice (or at minimum add dead declarations), diverging from every other Admin::AdminController subclass in the codebase and inviting confusion about where auth is enforced. The same duplication exists in Admin::EmbeddingController.
raw_findings.root_cause: Filters copied into subclasses that already inherit them from Admin::AdminController.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the redundant `ensure_logged_in`/`ensure_staff` declarations from both new controllers, keeping only `before_filter :fetch_embedding` where needed.
raw_findings.title: Redundant ensure_logged_in/ensure_staff filters duplicate Admin::AdminController behavior
raw_findings.trigger: Any request to the new admin controllers; Admin::AdminController already declares `before_filter :ensure_logged_in` and `before_filter :ensure_staff`.

raw_findings.body: The specs pass regardless of controller behavior; broken CRUD actions for the new embedding admin UI would not be caught by CI.
raw_findings.evidence:
it "is a subclass of AdminController" do
    expect(Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)
  end
raw_findings.failure_mode: Regressions in the new admin endpoints ship undetected.
raw_findings.impact: The specs pass regardless of controller behavior; broken CRUD actions for the new embedding admin UI would not be caught by CI.
raw_findings.root_cause: New behavior-bearing controllers were introduced with inheritance-only smoke specs.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add logged-in-admin request specs exercising create/update/destroy (including missing ids and blank category_id fallback) for both new controllers.
raw_findings.title: New admin controller specs only assert class inheritance, leaving all endpoints untested
raw_findings.trigger: Any regression in create/update/destroy of EmbeddableHostsController (or show/update of EmbeddingController) — e.g. the nil-record 500s or param handling — runs with zero spec coverage.

raw_findings.body: The assertions coincidentally pass against fruit 1's colors, so the test misdescribes what it verifies and would silently mask a bug where the wrong record is fetched or hydrated.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test asserts data for a different record than it claims to fetch, weakening coverage.
raw_findings.impact: The assertions coincidentally pass against fruit 1's colors, so the test misdescribes what it verifies and would silently mask a bug where the wrong record is fetched or hydrated.
raw_findings.root_cause: Test id changed to 2 without updating the fixture handler that ignores the id.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either make the pretender return the fruit matching `request.params.id` or change the test back to `store.find('fruit', 1)` so the asserted colors match the requested record.
raw_findings.title: 'find embedded' test requests fruit 2 but asserts fruit 1's data due to pretender fixture
raw_findings.trigger: The pretender handler for `/fruits/:id` always returns `fruits[0]` (fruit id 1, color_ids [1,2]) regardless of the requested id, while the test asks for fruit 2 (color_ids [3]).

raw_findings.body: Dead client action paired with a server PUT endpoint that performs no update — confusing surface area suggesting a save capability that does not exist.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unreachable/no-op code paths mislead maintainers about the feature's behavior.
raw_findings.impact: Dead client action paired with a server PUT endpoint that performs no update — confusing surface area suggesting a save capability that does not exist.
raw_findings.root_cause: Placeholder save plumbing committed without any template hookup or server-side persistence.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the unused `saveChanges` action and the no-op PUT `customize/embedding` route/action, or implement the actual settings persistence they imply.
raw_findings.title: saveChanges action is never wired to the embedding template and the server update is a no-op
raw_findings.trigger: Reviewing the new embedding admin screen: embedding.hbs contains only the addHost button, so `saveChanges` is unreachable, and Admin::EmbeddingController#update merely re-serializes @embedding without persisting anything.

validated_findings.body: `execute(...)[0]` raises (IndexError/NoMethodError on nil) before the embeddable_hosts branch is even reached, aborting the migration and blocking deploys for the common case of sites that never set embed_category.
validated_findings.evidence:
category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c
                        INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name
                        WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i
validated_findings.failure_mode: Migration raises and fails on sites without an embed_category setting row.
validated_findings.impact: `execute(...)[0]` raises (IndexError/NoMethodError on nil) before the embeddable_hosts branch is even reached, aborting the migration and blocking deploys for the common case of sites that never set embed_category.
validated_findings.root_cause: Unconditional indexing of a query result that can legitimately be empty.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Guard the result set: fetch the rows, and only call `['id'].to_i` when `cmd_tuples > 0` (mirroring the guard used for `embeddable_hosts` below), falling back to the uncategorized category id otherwise.
validated_findings.title: Migration crashes when 'embed_category' site setting row does not exist
validated_findings.trigger: Running `rake db:migrate` on any site that never customized the `embed_category` site setting (settings are only persisted when changed from default), so the SELECT returns zero rows.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R9-R11 shows `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` with no guard for empty result. If embed_category setting doesn't exist, the SELECT returns zero rows and `[0]` returns nil, causing NoMethodError on `['id']`. The embeddable_hosts query at R18-19 uses `cmd_tuples > 0` guard but this query does not.

validated_findings.body: Rows are inserted verbatim (raw SQL skips the model's before_validation that strips `https?://` and paths), so `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` comparing `lower(host) = <uri.host>` never matches; embedding silently stops working for those hosts after the migration.
validated_findings.evidence: execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
validated_findings.failure_mode: Previously-working embed hosts are rejected as invalid referers after upgrading.
validated_findings.impact: Rows are inserted verbatim (raw SQL skips the model's before_validation that strips `https?://` and paths), so `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` comparing `lower(host) = <uri.host>` never matches; embedding silently stops working for those hosts after the migration.
validated_findings.root_cause: Data migration inserts via raw SQL without replicating the normalization the new model relies on for lookups.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize each value in the migration before inserting (strip `^https?://` and any trailing path), matching the model's before_validation behavior.
validated_findings.title: Migration copies raw host strings (with scheme/path) that bypass model normalization, breaking host matching
validated_findings.trigger: A site whose old `embeddable_hosts` setting contains entries with a scheme or path (e.g. 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234'), which the old `allows_embeddable_host?` explicitly supported by stripping the scheme before comparing.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R25 shows raw INSERT with `'#{h}'` where h comes from the old setting. The before_validation in EmbeddableHost strips scheme/path, but raw SQL bypasses this. record_for_host compares `lower(host) = uri.host` which won't match if stored value has scheme prefix.

validated_findings.impact: The interpolated INSERT statement becomes malformed (or executes unintended SQL), aborting the migration mid-run.

validated_findings.title: Migration interpolates setting-derived host string directly into SQL
validated_findings.trigger: The old `embeddable_hosts` site-setting value contains a single quote or other SQL metacharacter in one of its newline-separated entries.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line R25 shows `VALUES ('#{h}'...)` with direct string interpolation. If h contains a single quote, the SQL becomes malformed. No escaping via quote() or parameterized query is used.
